work_order.understanding: Issue #28 collects eight findings against the release-notes gate shipped in PR #19 (merged, for #17). Against the code on main they resolve into four groups, three of which are code defects. Two crashes share one root cause in one function: reportError does unguarded I/O and throws instead of reporting. validateFile renders a non-person author with a bare JSON.stringify, so a self-referential YAML anchor (`authors: &a [*a]`) escapes the gate as an uncaught TypeError with no ::error:: line and no file name; and reportError reads upcoming-release-notes/README.md and writes process.env.GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY unconditionally, so a PR that deletes the README dies with ENOENT and a local run dies with ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE — precisely the failure mode the shipped AC-9 claimed to eliminate. Two honesty defects sit in the diff layer: SELECTED_STATUSES names 'C' while the invocation passes no copy-detection flag, so no C row is ever emitted and a unit test asserts against unreachable input; and the comment over core.quotePath=false claims git quoting is handled when the flag only suppresses octal-escaping of non-ASCII bytes — git still double-quotes any path holding a quote, backslash or control character, and the selector splits on tabs, so such a row is silently dropped and the branch reads as 'No release note added'. The largest finding (commit 3b7ff1a made four undescribed changes) is no longer actionable now the PR is merged — both its remedies are impossible — and its substantive residue is exactly the README sink, the quotePath overclaim and the unreachable C branch, all fixed here. The remaining two findings are not code defects and are recorded rather than 'fixed': the success message counts changed rather than added, which is the truthful count so the old AC-8 was wrong; and the missing [AI] PR-title prefix is a one-command process lapse, not a work order.
work_order.root_cause:
Three distinct causes, one per defect.

(1) Totality was claimed for findNonPersonAuthors but only delivered there. That function is total over YAML flow-sequence values and correctly returns a self-referential array as an offender; the call site at release-notes-check.mjs:77 then renders it with `typeof a === 'string' ? a : JSON.stringify(a)`, which throws on any structure containing a cycle. An author denylist's whole job is to survive whatever a PR author writes into the front matter.

(2) reportError treats its environment as guaranteed. The README is excluded from validation, so it is exactly the file a PR is most likely to delete, and it is read without a guard. GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is a runner-provided variable — always set inside Actions, absent on every local run — and is handed to fs.createWriteStream without a guard. Both throw synchronously out of a function whose contract is 'print an error and exit 1'.

(3) The diff layer parses a git output format only git can read unambiguously, then documents the ambiguity away. Tab-separated --name-status requires git to quote any path it cannot emit raw; core.quotePath=false suppresses only the octal-escaping of non-ASCII bytes and leaves the quoting rule intact, so a path containing a quote or control character arrives quoted and backslash-escaped, and selectReleaseNotePaths' split('\t') shreds it. Compounding it, SELECTED_STATUSES names a 'C' branch the invocation cannot produce, and a unit test asserts on it.
work_order.approach:
Four edits across two source files and one test file.

1. A non-throwing author renderer. Add `describeAuthor(value)` to util.mjs beside sanitizeWorkflowCommandData: return the string unchanged for strings, otherwise JSON.stringify inside a try/catch falling back to Object.prototype.toString.call(value). The `??` on the stringify result matters — JSON.stringify(undefined) returns undefined rather than throwing, and an offender rendering as the empty string would print a misleading 'authors must be...' message naming nothing. release-notes-check.mjs:77 becomes `nonPersonAuthors.map(describeAuthor)`.

2. Guard both of reportError's writes. Read the README behind fs.existsSync and degrade a missing one to an empty notice; when GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is unset, print the error and the notice and exit 1 without writing a summary. Both preserve the existing exit-1-with-a-message contract. The step-summary guard is one line beyond the ticket's literal list, kept because it is the same defect on the adjacent line of the function already being edited.

3. Make the copy branch honest by deleting it, not by enabling it. Verified: with --find-copies-harder a byte-identical copy emits `C100` under the production --diff-filter=AMRC, `added` is derived from the status column alone, so added is empty and the gate would refuse a PR that legitimately copied a note with 'No release note added' — a PR that passes today. So 'C' comes out of SELECTED_STATUSES and --diff-filter, the copy test goes with it, and the comments crediting 'R and C' are corrected to rename-only. Rename detection needs no flag — diff.renames defaults on, confirmed: `git mv` yields R100 through the production invocation unchanged.

4. Read paths with -z, and delete the quotePath flag rather than narrowing its comment. Append `-z` to the diff invocation, drop `-c core.quotePath=false` and the comment above it, and rewrite selectReleaseNotePaths to walk NUL-separated fields — each record is `status\0path\0`, a rename or copy record is `status\0old\0new\0`, so the parser reads the status, consumes two path fields for R and C and one otherwise, and keeps the last consumed path. The '.md' and README filters are applied to the single collected list BEFORE it is split into `added` and `changed`, so both are filtered identically; filtering only `changed` leaves the README and non-markdown paths in `added`, which silently reinstates the bug the filter exists to prevent. `added` is rows whose status is exactly 'A'. Doc comment rewritten to state the NUL contract and that both lists share the filters.

files.change: Three edits. (1) SELECTED_STATUSES becomes ['A','M','R'], its comment replaced to say a rename is selected because HEAD holds the new path and that no copy status is listed because the invocation asks for no copy detection, so git reports a copy as an addition — already selected. (2) Add exported describeAuthor(value) after sanitizeWorkflowCommandData: string passthrough, otherwise JSON.stringify inside try/catch with `?? Object.prototype.toString.call(value)`, plus a doc comment on why (a YAML anchor can make a value self-referential and JSON.stringify throws on a cycle; the ?? covers values JSON.stringify renders as undefined). (3) Rewrite selectReleaseNotePaths to parse NUL-separated `git diff --name-status -z` output: walk the fields with an index, skip empty fields, read the status, consume two path fields for R/C and one otherwise, keep the last consumed path, and collect the surviving rows. Apply the `.md` and README filters to that collected list once, then derive `added` as rows whose status is exactly 'A' and `changed` as every collected row — the filter must precede both, not apply to `changed` alone. Doc comment rewritten to state the NUL contract and the shared filter. Nothing else in the file changes.
files.why: Dropping 'C' removes a branch and a test that assert against unreachable production input; -z is the only form in which git emits paths verbatim, so it fixes the quote/backslash/control-character drop instead of documenting it, and retiring quotePath deletes the overclaiming comment rather than rewording it.

files.change: Five edits. (1) Import describeAuthor. (2) In reportError, replace the bare fs.readFileSync of README.md with a readmePath const behind fs.existsSync yielding '' when absent, and guard the summary write so an unset GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY prints the error and notice and exits 1 instead of calling fs.createWriteStream; keep the sanitize-then-print order and the exit-on-close behaviour for the guarded path. (3) Replace the author-rendering map with `nonPersonAuthors.map(describeAuthor).join(', ')`, dropping the inline typeof ternary. (4) The git argument array becomes exactly 'diff','--name-status','-z','--diff-filter=AMR',`origin/${baseRef}...HEAD`,'--',`${NOTES_DIR}/`; delete the `-c core.quotePath=false` pair and its three-line comment, and replace the diff-filter comment (currently crediting 'R and C') with one explaining the rename-at-new-path rule and the exclusion of deletions and copies. (5) Nothing else changes: category checks, one-line-body check, the existsSync guard, the missing-baseRef guard and the final success message stay as they are.
files.why: The two guards turn two synchronous throws inside a function whose contract is 'report and exit 1' into the gate's own message; describeAuthor closes the last path where a non-string author escapes as a stack trace; the -z switch makes the parsed path a real path rather than a quoted one.

files.change: Three edits. (1) Import describeAuthor and add a describeAuthor block covering string passthrough; int/float/null/true/empty map/nested list each rendered as their JSON form, byte-identical to the removed inline ternary; a self-referential array and a self-referential object both rendered without throwing; and undefined rendered as a non-empty string rather than ''. (2) Rewrite the selectReleaseNotePaths block so every fixture is NUL-separated, and delete the copy test outright so no C-row fixture remains in the file; keep the add, modify, rename, README/non-markdown/blank and ordering cases with existing expectations restated in NUL form, the ordering case keeping a D row to prove deletions are still filtered, and add a case pinning that the README and a non-markdown path are absent from `added` as well as `changed`. (3) Replace the café test, whose name and premise ('once git is told not to quote it') no longer hold, with verbatim-path cases for a non-ASCII filename, a double quote, a literal tab and a newline, each asserted to select as both added and changed. The findNonPersonAuthors and sanitizeWorkflowCommandData blocks keep every existing case verbatim.
files.why: A test asserting an unreachable input overstates coverage; a test whose name claims the flag fixed something it does not fix is the falsifiability gap. The self-referential cases make the call-site totality claim falsifiable rather than asserted, and the added-list filter case pins the one ordering mistake the new parser invites.

qa_script: 1. Unit suite. `yarn workspace @actual-app/ci-actions run test`. Baseline measured on main: 5 files / 54 tests green, util.test.js = 23. Expect green after the change with util.test.js's count higher than 23.

2. Build the sandbox once. `mkdir -p /tmp/rn28 && cd /tmp/rn28 && git init -q --bare origin.git && git clone -q origin.git work && cd work && mkdir -p upcoming-release-notes && printf 'See the docs.
' > upcoming-release-notes/README.md && printf -- '---
category: Maintenance
authors: [Shivam-Fl]
---
seed
' > upcoming-release-notes/seed.md && git add -A && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm base && git branch -M base && git push -q origin base`. The base branch must NOT be named main — the repo's git guard blocks a push to main. Write every scratch file OUTSIDE the work tree; untracked files in it abort the later `git checkout` and silently invalidate the run. Every step branches off `base` and runs `BASE_REF=base GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/rn28/s.md node <repo>/packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs` from inside /tmp/rn28/work. Run step 1 first so a dependency failure is not mistaken for a gate failure.

3. AC-1. `git checkout -q -B qa1 base && printf -- '---
category: Bugfix
authors: &a [*a]
---
selfref
' > upcoming-release-notes/qa-selfref.md && git add -A && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm qa1`. Expect exit 1, one ::error:: naming qa-selfref.md, and zero lines matching 'circular structure'.
4. AC-2. Same as step 3 with `authors: &a [{k: *a}]` on branch qa2. Expect the same, with no TypeError.

category: Nonsense
authors: [Shivam-Fl]
---
badcat
' > upcoming-release-notes/qa-badcat.md && git add -A && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm qa3`. Expect exit 1, the ::error:: about the category, and no 'ENOENT' anywhere in the output.

6. AC-4. `git checkout -q -B qa4 base && git rm -q upcoming-release-notes/README.md && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm qa4`. Expect '::error::No release note added' and exit 1 with no ENOENT.

category: Nonsense
authors: [Shivam-Fl]
---
bad
' > upcoming-release-notes/qa-bad.md && git add -A && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm qa5`, then `env -u GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY BASE_REF=base node <gate>`. Expect the ::error:: line and exit 1, no ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE.

category: Maintenance
authors: [Shivam-Fl]
---
quoted
' > 'upcoming-release-notes/has"quote.md' && git add -A && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm qa6`. Expect 'Validated 1 release note(s).' and exit 0. Confirm the row with `git diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=AMR origin/base...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/ | cat -A` (expect an unquoted path) and, for contrast, the same command without -z (expect a quoted, escaped path).

11. AC-8. Branch qa9: filename `upcoming-release-notes/café-note.md`. Expect 'Validated 1 release note(s).' and exit 0.

12. AC-9. `git checkout -q -B qa10 base && cp upcoming-release-notes/seed.md upcoming-release-notes/qa-purecopy.md && git add -A && git -c user.email=a@b -c user.name=a commit -qm qa10`. Expect 'Validated 1 release note(s).' and exit 0. Confirm git emits `A` here with `git diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=AMR origin/base...HEAD -- upcoming-release-notes/ | cat -A`, and that adding --find-copies-harder to the same invocation turns it into C100 — which is why the C branch was dropped rather than enabled.

13. AC-10a. Branch qa11: `git mv upcoming-release-notes/seed.md upcoming-release-notes/moved.md` and add a valid qa-ok.md (category Maintenance, authors [Shivam-Fl], one-line body) in the same commit. Expect 'Validated 2 release note(s).' — moved.md and qa-ok.md — and exit 0. Branch qa12: add a note and `git rm` seed.md in the same commit, but make the two files genuinely DISSIMILAR — the added note must not resemble seed.md, or git reports a rename (R091/R067) instead of A+D and the branch is rejected as 'No release note added', which tests the rename path a second time and never reaches the deletion filter. Worked recipe: `printf -- '---
category: Features
authors: [Matt-Fidd]
---
completely unrelated sentence about something else entirely
' > upcoming-release-notes/qa-ok.md`. Expect 'Validated 1 release note(s).' and exit 0 — confirm with `git -c core.quotePath=false diff --name-status origin/base...qa12 -- upcoming-release-notes/` that the rows really are `A` and `D` before believing the result.
15. AC-11. Branch qa13: add one valid note and edit seed.md's body in the same commit. Expect 'Validated 2 release note(s).', not 'Validated 1'.
16. AC-12a. Branch qa14 with `category: Nonsense`. Expect exit 1 and a ::error:: naming the category list.
17. AC-12b. Branch qa15 with `authors: []`. Expect exit 1 and 'empty authors list'.
18. AC-12c. Branch qa16 with `authors: [claude]`. Expect exit 1 and the 'must be GitHub usernames of people' line, with the rendered author present and not empty.
19. AC-12d. Branch qa17 with a two-line body. Expect exit 1 and 'body should contain exactly one line'.

20. AC-13. Assert the three facts the criterion names, in this order: (a) `grep -n 'SELECTED_STATUSES = ' packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs` prints `const SELECTED_STATUSES = ['A', 'M', 'R'];`; (b) `grep -n 'diff-filter' packages/ci-actions/bin/release-notes-check.mjs` prints `'--diff-filter=AMR',`; (c) `grep -n 'C75\|C100' packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.test.js` returns nothing. Do NOT grep for a bare 'C' across the package — the parser is required to keep an R/C branch for field consumption, so such a grep would fail a correct implementation.

21. Sanity: `git grep -n 'quotePath' packages/ci-actions` returns nothing, and `git grep -n 'split(.\\t.)' packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs` returns nothing. Both hold against the amended AC-13, which no longer asserts anything about quoting. Also confirm the parser splits on NUL: `grep -n "split('\\0')" packages/ci-actions/src/release-notes/util.mjs` returns a hit.
residual_risks: The -z parser is the riskiest edit: its failure mode is not a loud crash but a gate that silently selects nothing, which reads as 'No release note added' and refuses every PR. Step 13/15 (a normal add+rename and add+modify branch, both expecting 'Validated N release note(s).') are the cheapest proof that ordinary selection still works — run them before believing the exotic filename cases.

A branch that only renames a note is still rejected with 'No release note added', because added counts only A rows. This is pre-existing and covered by a deliberately passing unit test, so this plan leaves it; it is listed in unknowns as a separate decision, not a defect carried forward silently.

The .md and README filter must be applied to the collected list before it is split, not to `changed` alone. Filtering only `changed` puts the README and non-markdown paths back into `added`, which both lets a README-only edit satisfy the 'did this branch add a note' check and then validates the README as a note. I hit exactly this while prototyping the parser; the new unit case pins it, but it is the one place the rewrite can silently regress.

parseReleaseNotes in the same module still renders authors as `@${a}` with no guard, so a note carrying a self-referential anchor could reach the docs generator. Template interpolation of a circular array does not throw, so it degrades rather than crashes — but it is a second renderer this plan does not cover, and the gate is the only place that rejects such a note today.

The gate still exits 1 on a stack trace if reportError's own write to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY fails (a full disk, for instance): the exit happens on the stream's 'close' event and there is no 'error' handler. Pre-existing, not on the ticket, and not reachable in Actions.

A filename holding a control character other than tab or newline now arrives at the error path as a real path. sanitizeWorkflowCommandData escapes CR and LF, so a newline cannot break the ::error:: annotation, but the raw path is still written into the log by other means. Verbatim parsing is strictly better than dropping the row, and no such filename is known to exist.

alternatives_considered.approach: Enable the copy branch with -C / --find-copies-harder, as the review's first suggestion for the unreachable C row offers.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Verified to introduce a false failure rather than close a coverage gap. With copy detection on, a byte-identical copy emits C100 under --diff-filter=AMRC; added is derived from the status column alone, so added is empty and the gate refuses the PR with 'No release note added'. The same PR emits A and passes today. It also costs rename/copy detection across the whole diff for no security gain.

alternatives_considered.approach: Narrow the quotePath comment to what the flag actually fixes and leave the parser on tab-separated output, as the review's first suggestion for the quotePath finding offers.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It documents the bug instead of removing it, and leaves in place a flag whose stated purpose the repo has now got wrong twice. -z is a one-argument change to the invocation plus a rewrite of one small parser, and I verified it fixes quote, tab and newline filenames while retiring the flag outright.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make the check script testable by extracting validateFile and reportError, so each failure path gets a unit test instead of a sandbox recipe.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The script is top-level and side-effecting by construction — it reads env, runs git and exits the process — and the previous PR already moved the pure logic into util.mjs for exactly this reason. Restructuring is a rewrite well beyond four findings, and the behaviours that matter (an uncaught throw reaching stderr, an exit code) are only observable end to end anyway.

alternatives_considered.approach: Wrap reportError's body in a try/catch, or install a process-level uncaughtException handler, to convert any throw in the reporting path into a clean exit 1.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It hides the defect rather than fixing it: the gate would exit 1 with a correct code and a silently swallowed error, and the next unguarded I/O would be invisible instead of loudly failing a test. Two explicit guards say what they assume and why, and each is its own falsifiable criterion.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a catch-all around the author list — JSON.stringify with a WeakSet-aware replacer, or render every offender as just its typeof.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A replacer still walks the structure and still has to be reasoned about; typeof alone throws away the information the author needs to fix their note. The try/catch plus Object.prototype.toString fallback is three lines, terminates on every value I constructed (including bigint and symbol, which I also checked), and keeps the exact rendering every non-circular shape had before.

alternatives_considered.approach: Handle the self-referential case inside findNonPersonAuthors, returning a normalised string per offender instead of the raw value.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: findNonPersonAuthors is total and correct today, and its existing unit tests pin it to returning the raw offending values. Folding rendering into it would change a function with one caller and require all twelve existing cases rewritten, to fix a bug that is not in it.

alternatives_considered.approach: Leave the success message alone and write the old criterion as 'Validated 1 release note(s)' with the added-length recipe.

work_order.debate_summary:
There was no debate to arbitrate: plan/critique.json is `{}` — the critic stage produced no findings at all — so I had nothing to judge, dismiss or fold in. I planned the issue from plan/brief.md and the code, and independently reproduced every runtime claim rather than taking the rejected plan's evidence section on trust. All six load-bearing reproductions held exactly as described: the self-referential list throws TypeError at line 77 with zero ::error:: lines; the self-referential map throws the same error and is genuinely a distinct code path (the stack reports a cycle through an Object rather than an Array); the deleted README throws ENOENT out of reportError on both its call sites; GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY unset throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE once the README read is out of the way; a quote in a filename emits a quoted, backslash-escaped row and the gate reports 'No release note added'; and with -z the same row arrives verbatim. I also confirmed the decision the plan is built on is the right way round rather than the reverse: the production filter emits A for a byte-identical copy and the gate passes, while adding --find-copies-harder to the identical tree emits C100 — so enabling copy detection really would empty `added` and fail a PR that passes today. The baseline is 5 files / 54 tests with util.test.js at 23, as claimed. I wrote the NUL parser and describeAuthor as a prototype and ran them against 27 inputs; after one correction they all behave as specified.

What I corrected against the rejected plan. (a) The brief's review rejection is binding and I implemented it: AC-13 no longer asserts that 'no code path names a copy status', because the parser must keep an R/C branch — field consumption happens before the status filter, so a C record parsed with one path would desynchronise every record after it. AC-13 now asserts three checkable facts (the SELECTED_STATUSES literal, the --diff-filter argument, and no C fixture in the test file), and qa_script step 20 asserts those three directly instead of grepping for 'C' across the package, which a correct implementation would trip. I verified each grep against the pre-change tree so the step is known to be satisfiable. Step 21's quotePath and split('\t') assertions still hold against the amended criterion, and I added a positive NUL-split assertion to it. (b) My prototype's first version applied the '.md'/README filter to `changed` only, which put the README and non-markdown paths back into `added` and made the AC-10b-style case fail. That is the single most likely way to get this rewrite wrong, so files[] now states the filter must precede the split, the approach says why, a new unit case pins it, and it leads the residual risks. (c) The rejected plan's qa_script step 14 could not have tested what it claimed: adding a note and deleting seed.md with near-identical content makes git report R091/R067, not A+D, so the branch is rejected as 'No release note added' and the deletion filter is never exercised. I hit this myself, worked the recipe with a dissimilar note until it produced genuine A and D rows, and AC-10 plus step 14 now carry the requirement to confirm the rows really are A and D before believing the result. (d) AC-14 no longer asserts case-count arithmetic that does not reconcile with the case list; it states the falsifiable property — green, count above 23, only the copy and café cases removed.

Where I kept the rejected plan's judgement calls and disagree with the reviewer: dropping 'C' rather than enabling copy detection, and taking -z over merely narrowing the comment. Both are the load-bearing decisions and I verified the reviewer's own first suggestions are wrong on the merits. The review also asked for a scope split; I declined it — all four defects are in the same two files and all four came from one review pass, and splitting would leave the tree in the state the issue complained about for longer. I am recording that refusal rather than burying it.

The honest caveat, and it is the same one the rejected plan recorded about itself: with an empty critique, the only counterweight to my judgement is my own reproduction. It held on everything I checked, but 'the author verified it and the arbiter verified it again' is weaker evidence than an adversarial pass from a third party. Three judgement calls remain genuinely open — whether the maintainer wants rename support at all, whether quote/tab filenames are considered impossible by policy, and whether the GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY guard belongs in scope at all — and I have put all three in unknowns rather than pretending they are settled. Each is cheap to reverse before code is written.
work_order.confidence_rationale: Every runtime claim reproduced for me independently in a clean sandbox repo with a controllable origin, not taken from the rejected plan's word: both self-referential author shapes throw at line 77 with zero ::error:: lines; the deleted README throws ENOENT on both reportError call sites; an unset GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE once the README read is out of the way; a quote in a filename is dropped as 'No release note added' with the raw row captured; a byte-identical copy emits A under the production filter while --find-copies-harder emits C100, so the load-bearing decision to drop 'C' rather than enable it is verified in both directions; and -z emits the quote path verbatim. I also confirmed the R100 record needs no flag, the call graph has no second consumer of the parser, and the 5-file/54-test baseline. I built the proposed parser and describeAuthor as a prototype and ran them against 27 inputs, which is how I found the filter-ordering trap and the broken AC-10b recipe — both are now pinned by criteria and tests. What holds this under 90: the -z layout was exercised on this machine's git rather than on the runner images Actions ships, which is the single assumption most likely to be wrong; the parser rewrite is the riskiest edit and its failure mode is a gate that quietly refuses every PR, which is why the ordinary-selection steps lead the residual risks; and three scope judgements (rename support, exotic filenames, the step-summary guard) are ones a maintainer may reasonably reverse. I scored 87 rather than lower because nothing load-bearing is a guess — every claim I could test, I tested — and I scored it below 90 for the runner-image gap and the open scope calls.
evidence: AC-1 reproduced against main: front matter `authors: &a [*a]` with a one-line body produced zero ::error:: lines and `TypeError: Converting circular structure to JSON` at JSON.stringify, called from release-notes-check.mjs:77:53 inside Array.map inside validateFile, exit 1.

AC-2 reproduced against main independently: `authors: &a [{k: *a}]` throws the same TypeError at the same line, the cycle reported through an Object rather than an Array, confirming the map shape is a distinct path the list case does not cover.

AC-3 reproduced against main: with README deleted and a note carrying `category: Nonsense`, the ::error:: category line, then `Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open 'upcoming-release-notes/README.md'` at release-notes-check.mjs:34 inside reportError, exit 1.

AC-4 reproduced against main: with README deleted and no note added, the same ENOENT out of reportError via the `added.length === 0` call site, exit 1 — a different call site from AC-3, so both are covered.

AC-5 reproduced against main only once the README read was out of the way: with the README present and an invalid category, `env -u GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` gives `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]` from node:internal/fs/streams at release-notes-check.mjs:37, exit 1. My first attempt at this was invalid — deleting the README let AC-3's ENOENT fire first and mask it; the qa script keeps the README present for this step.

AC-6 reproduced end to end against main: a note committed as `upcoming-release-notes/has"quote.md` gives exit 1 with 'No release note added', and the raw row under the production invocation is `A\t"upcoming-release-notes/has\"quote.md"` — quoted and backslash-escaped even with core.quotePath=false, so the tab-split selector drops it. The same row with -z is `A\0upcoming-release-notes/has"quote.md\0`.

AC-7 reproduced against main: filenames built with `$(printf 'upcoming-release-notes/tab\there.md')` and `$(printf 'upcoming-release-notes/nl\nname.md')` each give exit 1 with 'No release note added'.

AC-8 already passes on main (exit 0, 'Validated 1 release note(s).') because core.quotePath=false does suppress the octal-escaping — so this criterion is a regression guard on deleting the flag, not a fix. Confirmed the -z row for the café path is `A\0upcoming-release-notes/cafM-CM-)-note.md\0`, unescaped.

AC-9 verified both halves against main with the production filter: a byte-identical copy under `--diff-filter=AMRC` emits `A\tupcoming-release-notes/qa-purecopy.md` and the gate passes with 'Validated 1 release note(s).'; adding --find-copies-harder to the same tree emits `C100\tupcoming-release-notes/seed.md\tupcoming-release-notes/qa-purecopy.md`. Since added is derived from the status column alone, enabling copy detection would empty added and fail the PR. Also confirmed the R branch is reachable today with no flag: `git mv` yields R100 through the unchanged production invocation.

The proposed NUL parser run against 15 inputs: add, modify, rename (binds new path, not added), delete, a C row, README, non-markdown, blank, quote, tab, newline, non-ASCII, output with no trailing NUL, and multi-record input. My first version applied the '.md'/README filter to `changed` only and returned the README and notes.txt in `added` — the test caught it. With the filter moved ahead of the split, all 15 pass, including a C row followed by an A row, which is the case that proves a C record cannot desynchronise the records after it.

The proposed describeAuthor run over twelve values: string, int, float, null, true, empty map and nested list all render byte-identical to the old inline ternary; undefined, both self-referential shapes, bigint and symbol all render non-empty without throwing.

Callers enumerated by grep across the repo: util.mjs is imported by release-notes-check.mjs, release-notes-generate.mjs and packages/docs/scripts/generate-upcoming-release-notes.mjs; the latter two import only parseReleaseNotes and formatNotes, both untouched. The check script is invoked only from .github/actions/release-notes/check/action.yml, which sets BASE_REF and nothing else — GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is supplied by the runner, confirming AC-5 is a local-run criterion.

Baseline measured: `yarn workspace @actual-app/ci-actions run test` is green on main at 5 files / 54 tests, with util.test.js contributing 23 — matching the rejected plan's claim, and 23 `it(` blocks counted directly in the file.

AC-13's corrected greps checked against the pre-change tree so the step is known to be satisfiable: SELECTED_STATUSES currently reads ['A','M','R','C'] at util.mjs:37, --diff-filter currently reads AMRC at release-notes-check.mjs:104, and the C fixture currently sits at util.test.js:133 — three named lines an implementer changes and QA re-checks, rather than a bare 'C' grep the parser's required R/C branch would trip.

Findings on commit 3b7ff1a are no longer actionable now the PR is merged and issue #17 closed: the work order it was reviewed against cannot be amended and the commit cannot be split, so both of its own remedies are impossible. Its four substantive sub-items are exactly the README sink, the quotePath flag, the AMRC filter and the selectReleaseNotePaths extraction, all covered by this change.
